data.content_ref: inline:{"claim": "Two conclusions are the same claim iff they originate from the same triggering query or goal and occupy the same position in the reasoning plan.", "mechanism": "The system tags each conclusion with its causal ancestry: the top-level query and the path of subgoals. When two conclusions agree, it checks if their ancestry tags match. If so, they are the same claim; otherwise, they are contextually distinct.", "scope": {"covers": ["goal-directed reasoning systems with explicit query tracking"], "excludes": ["bottom-up or forward-chaining systems without goal tags"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two conclusions with identical ancestry tags are treated as distinct", "eval": "program:causal_ancestry_check"}, {"case": "Two conclusions with different ancestry tags are merged", "eval": "program:causal_ancestry_check"}], "prose_notes": "Identity is relative to the reasoning context. Eager merging across contexts risks context collapse; reluctance misses cross-contextual generalizations."}
